measure: The inspector reads over the corpus. Per repository and selection, two analyses through the real AnalysisRegistry (RegistrySettings.production, Stages.production()) on fresh data directories. After the terminal event, with the registry open, every request goes through a Dispatcher built on Handlers.all and the production JsonLines.Writer into a buffer (Lifecycle's path for one frame, without stdin and the pipe). Both analyses: the IT's SQL census; the SWEEP, recorded as a transcript (per internal PACKAGE and TYPE in code-point order: element.describe, then element.dependencies IN and OUT at limit 1); then the worst requests in a second transcript (level 1, the worst package's TYPE slice, the most-methods describe, the IN and OUT chains to the end at limit 500 and 2000, the three most-evidenced pairs). The second analysis asks the first's targets, and the transcripts compare byte for byte. Analysis 1 only: the IT's oracle SQL for the targets, then each worst request cold (first call on a fresh reader: the idle readers are discarded first by read units that throw, the production path that closes a reader after a failure) and nine times warm.

requests.element.dependencies: {analysisId, cursor?, direction, elementId, limit}; sweep limit 1, chains [500, 2000]

settings.cold: the first call on a fresh reader: every idle reader closed first through SqliteConnections.read's failure path, so the timed call opens a new SQLITE_OPEN_READONLY reader (its pragmas included) with an empty SQLite page cache; the OS page cache is not purged, the JIT is warm (the sweep ran first)

baselines.census: worst elements from an earlier analysis of the corpus, embedded as literals
baselines.cost: warm medians from an earlier cost probe, embedded

environment.storage: APPLE SSD AP1024Z internal NVMe SSD
environment.runtime: full JDK under Maven Surefire, not the jlink image the application ships

host.storage: APPLE SSD AP1024Z internal NVMe SSD
